column1: # Columns a Devanagari unit takes: baud-core's cursor advance (CPR) and what each program assumes.

# 404 units were measured: the README's Hindi line and its eight words, the Devanagari examples of Microsoft's specification, and every word of two Premchand pages. That is the 399 distinct inputs of crates/baud-font/tests/shape/devanagari.txt, plus the five words of the README line that file does not list (हर, अक्षर, ग्रिड, रखता, है।).
# The README line and its words come first, then the file's other inputs in the order it first lists them.

# baud_one_cell is baud-core's cursor advance read back by CPR, legacy_cells and legacy_mc0 a prototype's by CPR with GB9a and GB9c (or GB9c alone) made cell breaks, cap2 computed as at most two; every other column is that program's own count for the unit.
